sources.title: EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC BLACK GAMING 12GB specification

findings: Four spring-loaded cooler mounting screws pass through the PCB around the GPU; the presenter uses a Phillips #0 driver.
Additional screws secure the fin-stack base and I/O/display bracket. These are distinct from the four GPU mounting screws; the video does not provide a fully calibrated board-wide screw map.
Both fan leads are separate connectors with release clips; disconnect before lifting the cooler.
technical_observations.limitations: The video does not enumerate every screw in the same grouping as Tom's Hardware's eight rear fasteners. Preserve the four GPU-area screws as a known subset; do not infer that every fan/shroud/port fastener is part of the eight.

findings: Two thermal-pad thickness observations are spoken: about 2.0 mm for one pad and approximately 1.5 mm for another; the second is explicitly described as harder to measure.
The presenter counts two central heatpipe tubes running through the GPU contact plate and estimates approximately 6 mm tube diameter.
The copper GPU cold plate contacts the die directly; it is joined to the fin stack, and the pipes return through the copper plate toward the memory-side region.
Six GDDR6 positions are visible, arranged three along one side and three along the other; some pipe runs cross the memory region without direct memory contact.
technical_observations.limitations: The narration does not assign the 2.0 mm and 1.5 mm observations to specific memory/VRM locations or package footprints. Heatpipe tube-loop count and exposed tube-run count are different possible counting conventions; do not collapse them without a drawing.

findings: The presenter identifies a row of MOSFETs contacted by a copper plate.
Two inductors are discussed on the opposite-side power area; the presenter tentatively calls that area the memory VRM, so that functional assignment remains tentative.
The presenter notes a thermal-pad impression on the two-inductor area but says the pad contact is incomplete for the rest of the nearby inductors.
Each fan is retained by three screws and has its own independently replaceable lead.
technical_observations.limitations: No MOSFET part number, inductor designation, inductance, VRM phase topology, controller identity, pad footprint or screw coordinates are provided.

findings: Two current-sense shunts are discussed: one associated with the auxiliary power-input path and a separate one associated with PCIe-slot 12 V.
The presenter states a 5 milliohm shunt on the auxiliary power-input path; do not copy that value to the separate slot shunt.
A fuse is visible for input-protection troubleshooting.
The cleaned GPU die marking is read as NVIDIA GA106-300-A1.
technical_observations.limitations: The transcript does not provide fuse part number/rating, shunt reference designators, calibrated electrical nets or the resistance of the slot shunt.

sources.title: EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC Black Gaming Review
EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC teardown with 12G-P5-3655-KR sample label
sources.applicability: The article body describes an EVGA RTX 3060 XC teardown. The rear-PCB identity photograph on the article's main page visibly reads P/N 12G-P5-3655-KR, the exact XC BLACK retail SKU. On the teardown page, Tom's Hardware reports eight cooler/shroud retention screws (four around the GPU and four near the far end), two fan connections, and six Samsung K4ZAF325BM-HC16 GDDR6 chips rated for 16Gbps. The photograph ties the teardown sample to the retail SKU; exact screw coordinates, package-to-net mapping and PCB revision remain unverified.
sources.identity_locator: Main review's EVGA rear-PCB photo: label reads P/N 12G-P5-3655-KR.

sources.title: EVGA232 / PG190-A02 GA104-GA106 GPU schematic — unverified community-hosted candidate
sources.applicability: The community file name includes EVGA232 / RTX 2070 / RTX3060 / PG190-A02 / GA104-GA106, but the document text itself carries NVIDIA drawing number 600-1G190-BASE-A02, PCB revision PG190-A02 and BOM revision A dated 2020-06-12. Its text-layer block diagram lists NVVDD-PH1 through PH8 and FBVDDQ-PH1/PH2; this is a reference-board topology only. The PDF does not mention retail SKU 12G-P5-3655-KR or the EVGA232 silkscreen. It must not be used to assert phase count, net routing, values or pinout for the XC BLACK until a physical-board correlation is established. Rendered-page screenshots could not be fetched during this audit, so no page artwork or component-value extraction is claimed.
sources.use_policy: Reference-only. Do not use its reference design to populate the exact EVGA XC BLACK VRM phase count, component inventory, PCB routing, BOM or service map. The title of a third-party index is not proof of board equivalence. No PDF pages or third-party assets are redistributed.
